# Overview

Multi-omics studies often run several assay platforms on the same subjects,
for example RNA-seq, miRNA-seq and a protein array on the same tumours. Each
platform gives an **assay block**: all features that platform measures for a
subject. In practice not every subject has every block. A sample can be used
up, an assay can fail, or a platform may have been run on only part of the
cohort, so a subject ends up missing a whole block at once. This is
*block-missingness* (the data are "ragged"). It differs from feature-level
missingness, where a few values are absent inside an otherwise measured
block.

Methods differ in how they treat such subjects:

* **DIABLO** (Singh et al. 2019, in the mixOmics package) is supervised but
  needs every subject to have every block, so subjects missing a block are
  removed before the analysis.
* **MOFA2** (Argelaguet et al. 2020) accepts samples with whole views missing
  (coded as `NA`), but it is unsupervised: its factors are not steered
  towards a class label.
* **missRows** (Voillet et al. 2016) handles missing individuals in multiple
  factor analysis by multiple imputation of the missing rows (MI-MFA), then
  combines the imputed analyses. It is unsupervised and fills in the missing
  blocks.

**woven** (Weighted Omics View Embedding via Nystrom) is supervised, like
DIABLO, and keeps subjects with missing blocks, like MOFA2 and missRows, but
it does not impute the missing blocks. It fits a shared latent space on the
**anchor subjects** (those observed in every block) and then scores every
other subject from the blocks it has, using the projection matrices learned
on the anchors. Compared with missRows, woven therefore adds supervision by
the outcome and avoids imputing whole blocks; compared with MOFA2 it adds
supervision; compared with DIABLO it keeps the incomplete subjects.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Assay block, modality | All features from one platform for one subject. |
| Block-missing, ragged | A subject lacks one or more whole blocks. |
| Anchor subjects | Subjects observed in every block; the model is fitted on them. |
| SUMCOR | "Sum of correlations" multi-set canonical correlation analysis: it finds latent scores, one set per block, that maximize the summed pairwise correlation between blocks. woven solves it in closed form with one eigendecomposition. |
| Label-augmented cross-covariance | The class labels are added to the between-block cross-covariance, so the latent directions are both shared across blocks and class-discriminative. |
| Graph Laplacian | A k-nearest-neighbour graph per block that keeps subjects that are similar in that block close in the latent space (`lambdas` sets its weight). |
| Nystrom extension | A way to place new points in an already fitted embedding without refitting it (Bengio et al. 2004). For woven's linear embedding it is the projection itself: a subject's observed features times the projection matrices. |
| ESS retention | Effective sample size retention, the fraction of subjects a method can score (`woven_ess_retention()`). For woven it is the fraction with at least one observed block; for a complete-case method it is the anchor fraction. |
| Nystrom (leave-anchor-out) error | `woven_nystrom_error()`: refit without one anchor, project it, and measure how far its score moves. Small values mean scores of unseen subjects are stable. |

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("woven")
```

# A real block-missing example: adrenocortical carcinoma

`r Biocpkg("MultiAssayExperiment")` is the Bioconductor container for several
assays on overlapping sets of subjects, and `woven()` takes one directly.
Each experiment becomes one block, subjects are aligned through the
`sampleMap`, and a subject with no sample in an experiment is treated as
missing that block.

The example uses `miniACC`, a subset of the TCGA adrenocortical carcinoma
(ACC) data distributed with MultiAssayExperiment (derived from
`r Biocpkg("curatedTCGAData")`). We keep three blocks, RNA-seq (198 genes),
miRNA-seq (471 miRNAs) and a reverse-phase protein array (RPPA, 33
proteins), and use the published C1A/C1B transcriptional subtype as the class
label.

```{r acc-load, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(woven)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
data(miniACC)

blocks <- c("RNASeq2GeneNorm", "miRNASeqGene", "RPPAArray")
acc <- miniACC[, !is.na(miniACC$C1A.C1B), blocks]
```

(Subsetting to three experiments makes MultiAssayExperiment warn that the
other two were dropped; that is expected.)

The sequencing counts are log-transformed; the RPPA data are already on a
log scale. `woven()` then standardizes every feature (`scale = TRUE`).

```{r acc-transform}
for (e in c("RNASeq2GeneNorm", "miRNASeqGene")) {
    acc[[e]] <- log2(assay(acc[[e]]) + 1)
}
acc
```

The RPPA array was run on only part of the cohort, so many subjects are
missing that block:

```{r acc-pattern}
table(sampleMap(acc)$assay) # samples per block
table(complete_in_all_blocks = complete.cases(acc))
table(acc$C1A.C1B)
```

## Fit

`Y` can be the name of a `colData` column.

```{r acc-fit}
fit <- woven(acc, Y = "C1A.C1B", K = 2L)
fit
```

## Scores map back to `colData`

`latent_scores()` has one row per subject, in the order of
`rownames(colData(acc))`, so the scores can be stored next to the clinical
data and used in any downstream model.

```{r acc-coldata}
scores <- latent_scores(fit)
identical(rownames(scores), rownames(colData(acc)))
colData(acc)$WOVEN1 <- scores[, 1]
colData(acc)$WOVEN2 <- scores[, 2]
head(as.data.frame(colData(acc))[, c("C1A.C1B", "vital_status", "WOVEN1")])
```

```{r acc-plot, fig.cap = "WOVEN latent space for the ACC tumours. Solid points are anchors; faded points are tumours without RPPA data, scored from RNA-seq and miRNA-seq."}
plot(fit, labels = acc$C1A.C1B)
```

## Coverage

```{r acc-coverage}
n_total <- nrow(colData(acc))
n_complete <- length(anchor_indices(fit))
n_scored <- sum(!is.na(latent_scores(fit)[, 1]))
data.frame(
    subjects = c(
        "complete-case (what a fully-paired method such as DIABLO uses)",
        "scored by woven"
    ),
    n = c(n_complete, n_scored),
    ESS = c(
        woven_ess_retention(n_complete, n_total),
        woven_ess_retention(n_scored, n_total)
    )
)
```

## Held-out prediction

The scores above are in-sample: the labels of these subjects were used to
fit the model, so their separation is optimistic. To see how the model does
on subjects it has not seen, fit on part of the cohort and predict the rest.
`woven_predict()` also accepts a MultiAssayExperiment.

```{r acc-holdout}
set.seed(10)
test_ids <- sample(rownames(colData(acc)), 25)
train <- acc[, setdiff(rownames(colData(acc)), test_ids)]
test <- acc[, test_ids]

fit_train <- woven(train, Y = "C1A.C1B", K = 2L, verbose = FALSE)
pred <- woven_predict(fit_train, test)
head(pred)

truth <- test$C1A.C1B[match(rownames(pred), rownames(colData(test)))]
has_rppa <- rownames(pred) %in%
    sampleMap(test)$primary[sampleMap(test)$assay == "RPPAArray"]
table(blocks = ifelse(has_rppa, "all three", "no RPPA"),
    correct = pred$predicted_class == truth)
```

This is one random split, shown to illustrate the workflow; a proper
estimate repeats it, for example with cross-validation, and refits the
model in every fold.

## Features

Projection matrices are linear, so each feature has a loading on each latent
dimension. `woven_plot_vip()` ranks features by a variable importance in
projection (VIP) score and `woven_plot_loadings()` shows signed loadings.

```{r acc-vip, fig.cap = "Top genes by VIP score."}
woven_plot_vip(fit, modality = "RNASeq2GeneNorm", n_top = 15)
```

```{r acc-loadings, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Top signed loadings on dimension 1 in each block."}
woven_plot_loadings(fit, dim = 1L, n_top = 8)
```

# Input as a list of matrices

Without a MultiAssayExperiment, pass a named list of matrices with subjects
in rows (in the same order in every matrix) and features in columns. A
subject missing a block has that whole row set to `NA`. The package ships a
small simulated example in this format (see `?woven_example`).

```{r list-fit}
data(woven_example)
lapply(woven_example$X_missing, dim)
fit_sim <- woven(woven_example$X_missing,
    Y = woven_example$Y, K = 3L,
    verbose = FALSE
)
fit_sim
```

## Pre-processing

woven expects pre-processed, approximately continuous data. Apply the usual
platform transform first; woven then scales each feature to unit variance.

| Platform | Typical pre-processing |
|---|---|
| RNA-seq (bulk) | `log2(CPM + 1)` or a variance-stabilizing transform |
| DNA methylation | M-values, `log2(beta / (1 - beta))` |
| Proteomics | `log2(intensity)`, normalized per sample |
| Metabolomics | `log2` transform |
| Microbiome | centred log-ratio transform |

Do not impute missing blocks; leave their rows as `NA`.

# Diagnostics

```{r metrics}
set.seed(1) # NMI uses k-means, which is random
woven_metrics(fit_sim, woven_example$Y)
```

`woven_metrics()` reports the silhouette width and Davies-Bouldin index of
the classes in the latent space, the normalized mutual information (NMI)
between k-means clusters and the classes, and ESS retention. Like the scores
themselves, these are computed on subjects whose labels were used in the
fit, so they describe the fitted space rather than held-out performance.

`woven_nystrom_error()` measures how stable the score of an unseen subject
is: it removes one anchor at a time, refits, projects the removed anchor and
reports the mean distance from its full-fit score.

```{r nystrom}
set.seed(1) # the held-out anchors are drawn at random
woven_nystrom_error(fit_sim, woven_example$X_missing, n_loo = 10L)
```

`woven_plot_variance()` shows how the canonical correlations are spread over
the latent dimensions, which helps when choosing `K`.

```{r variance, fig.cap = "Share of the squared canonical correlations per dimension."}
woven_plot_variance(fit_sim)
```

# Tuning

`gamma_y` sets the weight of the labels (0 gives unsupervised SUMCOR),
`lambdas` the weight of the graph Laplacians, and `ridge_w` and `screen_top`
control the projection matrices when a block has many more features than
there are anchors. Choose them by cross-validated classification error,
refitting within each fold. Graphs do not depend on these settings, so build
them once with `woven_precompute()` and pass them to every fit:

```{r precompute}
pc <- woven_precompute(woven_example$X_missing)
fits <- lapply(c(0.5, 5), function(g) {
    woven(woven_example$X_missing,
        Y = woven_example$Y, K = 3L,
        gamma_y = g, precomp = pc, verbose = FALSE
    )
})
vapply(fits, function(f) singular_values(f)[1], numeric(1))
```

`woven_precompute()` records whether it scaled the data, and `woven()`
stops if its own `scale` setting differs.

# Limitations

* woven is supervised. It needs a class label for every subject, and its
  latent space is built to separate those classes, so it is not a tool for
  discovering unlabelled structure. Separation measured on the subjects used
  to fit the model is optimistic; assess it on held-out subjects.
* The projection matrices are learned from the anchor subjects only, so the
  anchors must be representative of the cohort. If they differ
  systematically from subjects with missing blocks, the projections may not
  transfer.
* Scoring a subject from the blocks it has assumes that which blocks are
  missing is unrelated to the outcome beyond what the observed data explain
  (missing at random). If missingness depends on unobserved values, scores
  of incomplete subjects can be biased.
* The model is linear in the features. Nonlinear structure can be passed in
  through a precomputed kernel for the graph, but the projections stay
  linear.
* There should be clearly more anchors than latent dimensions (the package
  warns when there are fewer than `5 * K`), and each block's projection
  matrix has rank at most the smaller of its feature count and the number of
  anchors.

# Accessing results

The fit is an S4 object of class `woven`. Accessors return the main
results; `?"woven-class"` lists every slot.

```{r access}
dim(latent_scores(fit))
names(projection_matrices(fit))
dim(projection_matrices(fit)$RNASeq2GeneNorm)
length(anchor_indices(fit))
singular_values(fit)
```

New subjects are scored with `woven_scores()` and classified with
`woven_predict()`, from either a list of matrices or a MultiAssayExperiment.
